_comment: The capture case table. One entry per fixture the harness
can produce. Both drivers read this file, so a case is defined once and
captured on all three platforms.
Fields:
case          fixture id; becomes tests/fixtures/<component>/<case>/
component     git-refresh | subagent | notify | statusline
observable    this component's captured output
git_state     a name from states.json, or null for cases with no repo
payload       file fed on stdin, relative to tests/harness/
args          argv passed after the subcommand (notify only)
clock         pinned reference epoch; every mtime_offset is relative to it
notify_config config input, relative to tests/harness/
inputs        state files the case supplies, with their intended mtimes
platforms     where the observable exists at all; defaults to all three.
A case is skipped with a printed reason on any platform it
omits, never captured as an empty fixture — a silently
empty golden file is worse than a missing one, because
everything downstream then asserts against nothing.
platform_note why the `platforms` list is narrowed, and who owns closing it
expect_render whether a full render is expected (default true). Drives
the cache-miss assertion in both directions: a true
case must leave an output-cache file behind, and a false
one must not. Byte-diffing cannot tell a full render from a
served cache or an early exit — they produce the same
bytes, which is exactly how the nine-day cache-death
incident stayed invisible.
Paths in `target` and inside payload files use the placeholders {HOME},
{TMP} and {REPO}, always with forward slashes — the PowerShell scripts
reach the filesystem through .NET path APIs, which accept them, so no
driver has to JSON-escape a Windows backslash.
{SESSION} expands to the case's session id after the scripts' own
[^a-zA-Z0-9_-] sanitization, so a hostile id lands where the script would
actually put it rather than where the case author guessed.

_inputs_by_component: Applied to every case of that component before its own `inputs`, so the
render inputs that must be pinned are pinned once rather than
restated 16 times. The learned map is warmed here on purpose: an
unwarmed map makes window resolution fall through to the seed table and
then to the 200K default, which is a different code path from the one a

cases.why: The hook must delete exactly the git and output caches and leave the tasks feed — which is a data store, not a performance cache — alone.
A non-file-modifying tool must not invalidate anything.
A session id carrying `../` must produce no path outside the temp root. The observable is the whole temp-root diff, so an escape shows up as a deletion the fixture does not list.
Degraded input deletes nothing and exits 0.
The observable is the exact bytes written to the tasks feed, and the handler must print nothing so the default agent panel survives.

Pins the projection: all ten reader fields in emission order, unlisted fields dropped, an explicit null dropped rather than emitted as "", and falsy values kept. Field order is part of the observable because the feed's bytes are an input to the statusline's output-cache key — a reordering would miss the cache every tick while rendering identically.
A session with nothing running is a real state, not a degraded one: it writes an empty list rather than skipping the write and leaving stale rows on screen.

Malformed-tick isolation. A broken payload must leave the last good feed in place — the contract half that got the raw-tee prototype rejected in docs/performance.md §7, because a tee that overwrites on garbage silently drops the subagent rows until the next good tick.
No feed file is created from empty input.

cases.platform_note: The Windows *script* delivers entirely in-process — System.Media.SoundPlayer, SystemSounds, and the BurntToast module — so it spawns nothing a PATH shim can observe, and an empty capture would be indistinguishable from a notification that never fired. This was resolved: the port cannot call BurntToast in-process, so it raises the toast by invoking powershell.exe at its absolute path, which gives Windows an external observable for the first time. That observable has no script counterpart to be captured from, so it is asserted against a literal in tests/equivalence.rs instead. Windows sound stays in-process via winmm and remains unobservable by design.
cases.why: The observable is the command and arguments notify invokes, captured through the PATH shims.

With `sound: false` for the event, no sound helper is invoked at all. THE CAPTURE DOES NOT SHOW THAT, and is kept as the record of why. Both bash scripts read the flag as `jq -r '.[$e].sound // true'`, and jq's `//` yields its right-hand side when the left is `false` as well as when it is null — so `false // true` is `true` and muting has never worked on macOS or Linux. The flags gate delivery and the Product Contract wins on behaviour, so the port mutes correctly and this fixture is a divergence record rather than the port's target. tests/equivalence.rs names it in DIVERGENT_FIXTURES and asserts the required behaviour against a literal.
A repo with no index at all. Pins the outer `.git/index` guard, not the unborn-HEAD divergence — see git-unborn-head-staged for that.

The unborn-HEAD divergence, captured from the state that actually reaches it. bash renders no git segment; Windows renders the literal `HEAD`. Which one the binary keeps is recorded, and its expected output becomes a literal rather than either capture.
Every optional field absent — each row degrades on its own rather than blanking the line.

The fixture the binary's `self-check` subcommand compiles in and renders after installation. It is the only case with no repository, which is what makes it hermetic -- every other case's output depends on a git state the installing machine has no reason to have, and a self-check that consulted the real working directory would render a git row on a developer's machine and none on a server. With no transcript path and no model in the payload, the rendered box is a pure function of the payload, so the binary can reproduce it with no filesystem access at all.
Degraded input exits before the render, so no output cache may be written — asserting that is what distinguishes a correct early exit from a render that produced nothing.
The session id is still recoverable from the raw text, so unlike the empty case this one really does exercise the no-cache-written assertion.
§4 requires a 4-byte astral-plane character, not just CJK: gawk's old greedy extraction silently zeroed the token counts of lines containing one.

Inside the 10s freshness window, so the feed is a render input. `inputs/tasks-feed.json` MUST stay compact single-line JSON: the bash status line reads the feed with `IFS= read -r`, one line, because the handler only ever writes one line. Pretty-print it and bash reads `{`, fails the object check, and silently falls through to the transcript tier — which is what this case exists to distinguish it from.
Outside the window, so the same bytes must be ignored. Byte-diffing the fresh case alone cannot tell these apart — the stale path falls back to transcript parsing and can render identically.
